title: SKU certification catalog and onboarding runbook for HW-specific performance
creator: Riya Patel
description: Create a canonical SKU Certification Catalog and an operational onboarding runbook that standardizes how models are validated and published per GPU family (A100/H100/L40S/MI300). The catalog will capture deterministic benchmark signatures, quantization sensitivity notes, cold/warm startup envelopes, and required artifact links. The runbook will be the prescriptive sequence for model engineers to follow when bringing a new model or variant into production, including gating thresholds for auto-pin, rollback criteria, and publishing steps for the public performance profile manifest.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical SKU catalog (Confluence) exists and documents per-GPU baseline p50/p95 token latency, memory/KV footprint, and throughput for the representative sample suite
Runbook in docs repo with step-by-step checklist: calibration, microbench, full-sample regression, quant-sensitivity sweep, canary plan, and profile publication
Automation scripts (bench harness + signature generator) hooked to CI that produce a signed performance artifact for a model build
Gating thresholds defined: p95 latency regression <= 10% vs baseline OR a documented performance justification, memory delta <= 12% for pinned variant, and functional parity checks pass
Published performance manifest (JSON) created in artifact storage and a PR created to runtime-1.20 release branch with manifest reference
steps: Define representative sample suite for candidate model (short/medium/long sequences + streaming scenarios)
Run microbench across all target SKUs (A100/H100/L40S/MI300) with cold and warm traces; capture p50/p95, throughput, GPU memory, KV footprint
Execute quantization sensitivity sweep (FP16->INT8/GLM-Q configs) and record quality regression metrics against eval prompts
Generate deterministic signature artifact (bench harness output + model sha + hardware sku metadata) and store in S3/artifacts/perf-signatures
Run canary rollout simulation to estimate impact on latency SLO under 10/50/90% traffic mixes
Author runbook PR linking artifacts + suggested pin recommendation (auto-pin / soft-pin / no-pin) with rationale
Post-publication: schedule regression monitoring dashboard and create automated alert rules for signature drift > threshold
decisions: Choose to keep a single canonical representative sample suite per model family rather than exhaustive per-customer traces to keep onboarding time reasonable
Adopt asymmetric gating: stricter latency thresholds on latency-sensitive SKUs (H100/L40S) and slightly wider tolerance on MI300 for throughput-focused workloads
Require quantization sensitivity artifacts for any variant proposed to be published as an optimized runtime variant
Publish signed manifest JSON per model-variant that includes sku metrics and a human-readable runbook link rather than embedding runbook steps inline
progress_updates: 2026-02-26: Kickoff meeting with serving, infra, and ML-Ops. Assigned owners for benchmarking harness (ENG-31642 owner) and docs (Riya).
2026-03-02: Initial microbench script landed in bench-harness repo (PR #1823). A100/H100 runs completed for short-sequence suite. Early H100 warm p95 shows 8% delta vs baseline.
2026-03-05: Quant sweep prototype completed on L40S for INT8 profile. Observed a small quality regression on long-sequence prompts; flagged to research for selective quantization strategy.
2026-03-09: Signature artifact schema finalized (fields: model_sha, variant_tag, sku, p50_ms, p95_ms, kv_bytes, quant_profile, bench_commit, timestamp). Draft runbook outline pushed to docs PR #47.
2026-03-10: Canaries simulation added to CI job; failures observed when traffic bursts exceed 2x baseline on MI300 - follow-up to tune batching/coldstart hysteresis scheduled.

Security (Anika Bose): requested that the manifest include a signed checksum and that artifact storage ACLs be checked before publication
Runtime (Omar Haddad): asked for a mechanized rollback tag in the manifest to tie into the rollout controller
ML Research (Priya Menon): recommended adding a small adversarial prompt set to the sample suite to surface quality regressions post-quant
